subject.title: [Bug]: WebChat + New Session displays default model but inherits parent's model override

question: For a WebChat child session created from a parent with a user model override, should the product preserve inherited routing and show it, start independently at the configured default, or support an explicit child-level Default that blocks inheritance?
rationale: Merged work establishes that child sessions intentionally inherit runtime selection, but the current picker semantics make that inheritance invisible and prevent a displayed Default selection from reliably selecting the configured default.

options.title: Show inherited selection and add explicit default
options.body: Keep the existing child-session inheritance contract, label the effective inherited model in WebChat, and store a distinct child-level default choice when the user explicitly selects Default.

options.title: Make new dashboard sessions independent
options.body: Stop carrying parent model selection into ordinary New Session creation so a newly displayed Default always resolves from the configured agent default.

options.title: Keep hidden inheritance unchanged
options.body: Retain current behavior and document that a Default-looking child may route through its parent, accepting the mismatch and user-cost risk.

recommendation.title: Show inherited selection and add explicit default
recommendation.body: Keep the existing child-session inheritance contract, label the effective inherited model in WebChat, and store a distinct child-level default choice when the user explicitly selects Default.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history ties the original inheritance behavior to this contributor's feature work, making them the best evidence-backed routing candidate for the contract decision.
